content: 1. Simvastatin levels or effects are increased by clarithromycin due to inhibition of hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated because it significantly raises the risk of rhabdomyolysis. Avoid coadministration. 2. Clarithromycin increases the systemic exposure of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction necessitates avoiding the combination or using an alternative drug. Both clarithromycin and siponimod also prolong the QTc interval, further emphasizing the need to avoid coadministration or closely monitor the patient. 3. Vonoprazan, a weak CYP3A inhibitor, increases sirolimus levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin also increases sirolimus levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition, making this combination serious and requiring an alternative therapy. 4. Clarithromycin reduces the efficacy of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering colonic bacterial flora necessary for drug activation. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Clarithromycin increases the levels of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider alternative therapy if necessary. 6. Clarithromycin increases solifenacin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, making this combination serious and requiring an alternative therapy. 7. Clarithromycin increases sonidegib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Use an alternative drug or monitor closely. 8. Clarithromycin increases sorafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, necessitating the use of an alternative therapy. 9. Clarithromycin increases sotalol levels, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. 10. Sotrasib decreases vonoprazan levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. 11. Clarithromycin increases sparsentan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration upon resumption. Monitor closely. 12. St. John’s Wort decreases clarithromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Stiripentol, a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, interacts with clarithromycin, increasing its levels. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates coadministered with stiripentol for altered effects. Use an alternative therapy or monitor closely. 14. Clarithromycin increases sufentanil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentrations, leading to prolonged adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Clarithromycin increases sulbactam/durlobactam levels by inhibiting OATP1-mediated active secretion. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. Monitor closely if unavoidable. 16. Clarithromycin and sulfamethoxazole both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 17. Clarithromycin increases sunitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, necessitating the use of an alternative therapy. 18. Clarithromycin increases suvorexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 19. Vonoprazan increases tacrolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin also increases tacrolimus levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, requiring an alternative therapy. 20. Clarithromycin increases tadalafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration for pulmonary hypertension. For other uses, limit tadalafil to 5 mg/day or 10 mg every 72 hours. 21. Clarithromycin increases talazoparib levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. Adjust talazoparib dose after discontinuing P-gp inhibitors. 22. Clarithromycin increases tamoxifen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Clarithromycin increases tamsulosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. 24. Clarithromycin increases tasimelteon levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Tazemetostat decreases clarithromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Use an alternative therapy or monitor closely. 26. Tecovirimat decreases clarithromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Clarithromycin and telavancin both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 28. Clarithromycin decreases temocillin effects via pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown. 29. Clarithromycin increases temsirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. 30. Clarithromycin increases teniposide levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. 31. Clarithromycin increases terbinafine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Clarithromycin and tetrabenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. 33. Clarithromycin increases tezacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust tezacaftor dosage if coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 34. Vonoprazan increases theophylline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin also increases theophylline levels by decreasing metabolism, though the clinical significance is minor. 35. Clarithromycin decreases thiamine levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Thioridazine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. 37. Clarithromycin increases tiagabine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. 38. Clarithromycin increases ticagrelor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 39. Clarithromycin increases tinidazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Tipranavir increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and clarithromycin increases tipranavir levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. 41. Clarithromycin increases tisotumab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to MMAE, the active metabolite, raising the risk of adverse effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Clarithromycin increases tobramycin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Clarithromycin increases tofacitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce tofacitinib dose to 5 mg daily when coadministered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. 44. Clarithromycin increases tolterodine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. 45. Clarithromycin increases tolvaptan levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. 46. Topiramate decreases clarithromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 47. Clarithromycin increases topotecan levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. 48. Clarithromycin increases toremifene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. 49. Clarithromycin increases trabectedin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used, administer it one week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day before the next infusion. 50. Clarithromycin increases tramadol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Trazodone and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. 52. Clarithromycin increases triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. 53. Vonoprazan increases triazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin also increases triazolam levels, necessitating the use of an alternative therapy. 54. Clarithromycin and triclabendazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. 55. Trifluoperazine and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. 56. Clarithromycin and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
